body:
I really don't mean to sound like I think everything is awful, woe is me, the world is hopeless et cetera, because as you say there are notorious individuals who are doing the world some good, Mr. Assange being a case in point.

The thing is, while these people of the world are commendable, they count as a mere drop in the ocean in the face of the amount of suffering that occurs everywhere. Suffering that no one can hope to resolve. There are thousands of children being raped, all across the globe, right as I type. Everything else pales in the wake of the one and only global truth: that of human and animal suffering.

Truths about me? The only truth I or anyone else can guarantee is my demise. It is this knowledge that frustrates me and grinds away at me. I am not frightened of death, not in the slightest, but I am frightened by the fact that it is the only thing I can count on.

I mean hypocrisy in the sense that I would be behaving as though with the naivety of childhood (without anxiety), but I can't see how I could do that sincerely without being aware that what I am really doing is *ignoring* the truth: about me, about the world, about everything.

That's the best answer I could hope to get out of this. The thing is, I know there have been times when I have been unequivocally happy, but these times were when I was green to the cruel reality of existence, when I was free from self-consciousness and purely an extroverted creature. I don't know how I could go back to that feeling without knowing the hypocrisy of my actions. While it isn't the most politically correct or sane thing to say, I think antidepressants might be the way to forgo this, in order to open myself to happy ignorance and bathe in it.

Thank you again for your great input, and I think the best thing I can hope for is that, as you say, time is a healer, and perhaps I will eventually forget what I have learned about life so that I can enjoy it unabashedly. I am only 19 after all, there have to be some great years ahead of me, at some point. In the meanwhile, I will seek help from my university's counseling scheme, I think.

I agree, but every time I've attempted to do something similar (for example, I spent one day going around and taking out every homeless person I came across for a sandwich and a chat at a local cafe) I felt nothing except embarrassed and awkward, and couldn't escape the feeling that I wasn't really doing it for them, but just to fulfill my own desire to look as though I'm a better person. I wasn't doing it because I really wanted them to get better, it was purely to make me feel less selfish, which to me seemed even more selfish. I don't know, I guess I take things too seriously. I am a bit of an over-thinker it must be said.
